Nearly every box is a runtime process, plus one storage cylinder. 'Agent CLI' is an external actor with no code path, which is acceptable. There are no linked zoom-in views, and the relay and interpretation paths are only named in a footer.

Five nodes are enough to answer the question, and omissions are stated ('Outside this view: Hosted relay path…'). The token/cookie auth on the daemon's HTTP and WS endpoints (src/server/daemon.ts:513) is missing. That auth is the main trust control on a LAN path.

Every edge is labeled and states sync/async/local. The two separately started WS directions are drawn as separate arrows. The legend says dotted = local, but at this size dotted and dashed look almost the same, so 'local' rests on the text label. The long-poll ordering is explained only in a note, not on the diagram.

'Dev machine' and 'iPad' frames show the deployment split. The WS edges cross the LAN boundary without marking it as a network/trust edge or saying what is exposed (port, token). Managed vs self-hosted is described in text only.

Flow mostly runs left to right, but the two WS arrows cross each other diagonally between Daemon and iPad browser. The 'no daemon: locked I/O' edge loops over the top. Edge and note text is about 7–8px at 1194x834, which is hard to read. Most of the canvas is empty margin.

The key explains frames, box vs cylinder, and solid/dashed/dotted, and says arrows include responses. Everything is the same red, so line style is the only non-text cue, and dashed vs dotted can't be told apart at this size. Names match the code.

Three notes cover real failure modes: the long-poll timeout clamp, files.lock with the 503 and stale-lock handling, and a corrupt canvas that fails closed. The 800ms debounce is shown. Nothing covers daemon crash or reconnect, or what happens to unsaved edits during the debounce window.

The footer gives the date, revision dca6c85 plus local edits, says 'Owner: Unassigned', and says the live runtime was NOT verified. Most claims match the code. Capped at 3 because there is no production verification and no owner. One detail is off (see inaccuracies).
Read cold, the diagram explains the loop correctly. The small type and crossing WS arrows slow reading. The files-mode edge can be mistaken for a step in normal flow, though the note fixes that.

coldRead: You draw on a canvas in the iPad browser. Your edits go over a WebSocket to a Node daemon on the dev machine. The daemon holds the live state and saves it to .vibeprint/ JSON files in the repo after an 800ms debounce. The coding agent (for example Claude Code) runs an MCP server as a stdio child process. When the agent calls a sketch tool, the MCP server makes HTTP calls to the daemon to read the sketch, write marks, or long-poll /api/wait for new edits. The daemon pushes marks and chat back to the iPad over the WebSocket. If no daemon is running, the MCP server reads and writes .vibeprint/ directly under a file lock: it gives up with a 503 after 5s and removes locks older than 10s. If canvas.json is corrupt, the daemon refuses to overwrite it and asks you to restore it from git. The relay path for off-LAN iPads and model interpretation of sketches are out of scope.
inaccuracies: The long-poll note gives 'default 120s'. That is the daemon's default (src/server/daemon.ts:689, src/core/daemon-client.ts:114). The MCP wait tool itself says 'Default 50' with max 600 (src/mcp/server.ts:826), so the note misstates the timeout the agent actually uses.
The daemon's HTTP and WS endpoints need a token (header or HttpOnly cookie, src/server/daemon.ts:162,513). The diagram suggests any LAN client can talk to the daemon.

The legend says dotted = local, but the local edges (stdio, debounced save, locked I/O) are drawn in a style that can't be told apart from the dashed async WS edges at this size. Line style alone gives the wrong mode.
improvements: Make the text and arrows larger and fix the crossing: run the two WS arrows in parallel lanes between Daemon and iPad browser, and use the empty margin so labels are at least about 11px at 1194x834.
Show the LAN trust boundary on the WS/HTTP edges: daemon port and token/cookie pairing auth. Correct the wait timeout to the MCP default (50s, max 600s).

Make the line styles clearly different, or add a second cue such as color or arrowheads for local vs async vs sync. Mark the files-mode edge as a fallback, for example with a 'fallback' tag or a separate inset.
